claim: Rodemack is roughly 8 km / 9 minutes by car from Frisange.
quote: The driving distance between Frisange and Rodemack is 8 km. It takes approximately 9 minutes to drive from Frisange to Rodemack.

claim: Rodemack is a classified Plus Beaux Villages de France encircled by 700 m of 14th-century ramparts (6 towers, 6-9 m high), nicknamed 'La Petite Carcassonne lorraine'.
quote: 700 mètres de remparts... La Petite Carcassonne lorraine... 6 towers with arrow slits along the walkway

claim: Rodemack's draws include the Sierck fortified gate, a medieval garden, the 17th-century Chapel of Our Lady, and the 18th-century Church of St. Nicholas.
quote: 700 metres of 15th-century ramparts surround the village, and you enter this charming medieval village through the fortified Sierck Gate... 17th-century Chapel of Our Lady, and the 18th-century Church of St. Nicholas

claim: Thionville lies about 17 km (~20 minutes) by car from Frisange.
quote: The driving distance between Frisange and Thionville is 12 miles, and it takes approximately 20 minutes to drive. In kilometers, the distance from Frisange to Thionville is 17 kilometers.

claim: Thionville's Tour aux Puces is the 14-sided former keep of the Counts of Luxembourg, now an archaeology museum labelled Musée de France with free entry on the first Sunday of each month.
quote: The Tour aux Puces is the former keep of the castle that the Counts of Luxembourg erected in Thionville at the end of the 11th century, and is an original 14-sided structure

claim: Château de la Grange in Manom (Thionville area) is an 18th-century listed residence with period chandeliers, embroidered tapestries and gilded furniture set in a Prairial garden.
quote: The Château de la Grange immerses you in the heart of the 18th century, with its magnificent chandeliers, richly embroidered tapestries and gilded furniture

claim: The Hackenberg fortress at Veckring is about 26 km from Thionville, putting it ~40+ km from Frisange — out of the 30 km radius.
quote: de Thionville au Fort du Hackenberg 26 km

claim: Hackenberg is the largest publicly accessible Maginot Line fort with 10 km of galleries, 19 combat blocks, and 2.5-3 hour guided tours (FR/EN/DE) at a constant 12 °C.
quote: the largest fort of the Maginot line which is opened to the public... 10 km of galleries and 19 combat blocks... constant 12°C (54°F) year-round

claim: The renovated European Museum Schengen reopened in June 2025 with a modern multilingual permanent exhibition on the Schengen Agreement.
quote: The museum reopened in June 2025 after undergoing major renovation. The newly renovated Schengen Museum is located at the heart of the tri-border region between Luxembourg, France, and Germany

claim: Schengen sits at the Dreiländereck Lux/Fr/De Moselle tri-point where visitors can straddle borders and view interpretive panels; the historic MS Princesse Marie-Astrid on which the 1985 agreement was signed is moored nearby and open to visitors.
quote: The Dreiländereck (Three-Country Point) is the exact place where Luxembourg, France and Germany meet on the Moselle, where you can literally stand with a foot in two countries

claim: Schengen is roughly 20-25 km by road from Frisange, comfortably inside the 30 km radius.

The Markusberg-Stromberg trail above Schengen climbs through vineyards to a Luxembourg/France ridge with panoramic Moselle views over Sierck-les-Bains and a Notre-Dame des Sept Douleurs chapel viewpoint.
quote: The hiking route begins in the Markusberg vineyards and leads along ridge paths above the Moselle, partly through vineyards, until reaching the panoramic view from the French Stromberg overlooking Sierck-les-Bains

claim: The Roman Villa Borg in Perl, Saarland is the only fully restored ancient villa complex of its kind and draws about 50,000 visitors a year.
quote: As the only ancient villa complex to have been fully restored, it paints a vivid picture of life 2,000 years ago... drawing approximately 50,000 visitors annually

claim: Villa Borg's open-air museum features working reconstructed Roman baths (frigidarium, caldarium, tepidarium), gardens, a gatehouse and a Roman tavern, with seasonal Roman Days reenactments.
quote: The open-air museum at the Borg Roman Villa houses an archaeological collection, working ancient villa baths, gardens, a splendid gatehouse and a Roman tavern

claim: Driving Frisange to Borg/Perl is roughly 32 km / ~31 minutes — slightly over the 30 km guideline but within easy reach.
quote: The driving distance between Luxembourg to Borg is 20 miles, taking approximately 31 minutes to drive

claim: The Roman Villa Nennig houses a 160 m² mosaic of over 3 million tiles depicting amphitheatre scenes — one of the largest and finest Roman mosaics north of the Alps and rare in remaining at its original site.
quote: Measuring 160 square meters, it is made up of over 3 million tiles... North of the Alps, this mosaic is one of the very few that remained at their original site

claim: Villa Nennig is open Tue-Sun April-September (8:30-noon, 1-6 pm); closed Mondays and Dec-Feb, with a multimedia 3D reconstruction of the original villa complex.
quote: April – September: Tuesday to Sunday 8:30 am – 12 noon and 1 – 6 pm... Closed from December to February and on Mondays
